cases.name: distinct-pair
cases.description: Two fields from the same two-value list never coincide in a row
cases.config: <tdc><env count="40" seed="distinct-1" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="P"><distinct><gen name="A" type="text" value="X,Y"/><gen name="B" type="text" value="X,Y"/></distinct></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.A}}|${{P.B}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: distinct-two-groups
cases.description: Two independent groups each hold within a row
cases.config: <tdc><env count="25" seed="distinct-2grp" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="P"><distinct><gen name="F1" type="text" value="p,q"/><gen name="F2" type="text" value="p,q"/></distinct><distinct><gen name="L1" type="text" value="m,n"/><gen name="L2" type="text" value="m,n"/></distinct></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.F1}}${{P.F2}} ${{P.L1}}${{P.L2}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: distinct-leaves-outsiders-alone
cases.description: A field outside the group is left unconstrained
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="distinct-mixed" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="P"><distinct><gen name="A" type="text" value="X,Y"/><gen name="B" type="text" value="X,Y"/></distinct><gen name="C" type="text" value="X,Y"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.A}}${{P.B}}${{P.C}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-rearranges-a-tight-pool
cases.description: 20 unique rows out of a 4x8 pool a single draw could not arrange
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="u" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="K" uniq="true"><gen name="a" type="text" value="a1,a2,a3,a4"/><gen name="b" type="text" value="b1,b2,b3,b4,b5,b6,b7,b8"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{K.a}}-${{K.b}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-keeps-exact-shares
cases.description: uniq only rearranges, so a declared share stays exact
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="u-shares" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="K" uniq="true"><gen name="a" type="text" value="a1,a2" percent="25,75"/><gen name="b" type="text" value="b1,b2,b3,b4,b5,b6,b7,b8"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{K.a}}-${{K.b}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: env-uniq-across-sequences
cases.description: <uniq> at env level: the tuple of the wrapped sequences is unique across rows
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="env-u" local="en" mode="memory"><uniq><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="a1,a2,a3,a4,a5,a6"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="text" value="b1,b2,b3,b4,b5,b6"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{A}}-${{B}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: env-uniq-leaves-outsiders-alone
cases.description: a sequence outside the <uniq> wrapper keeps the values it drew
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="env-u2" local="en" mode="memory"><uniq><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="x,y,z,w,v,u"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="text" value="p,q,r,s,t,o"/></sequence></uniq><sequence name="C"><gen type="text" value="k1,k2"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}${{B}}|${{C}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: env-distinct-across-sequences
cases.description: <distinct> at env level: the wrapped sequences differ from each other on every row
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="env-d" local="en" mode="memory"><distinct><sequence name="Born"><gen type="text" value="Paris,Rome,Lyon"/></sequence><sequence name="Lives"><gen type="text" value="Paris,Rome,Lyon"/></sequence></distinct></env><block><line><data>${{Born}} -> ${{Lives}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: env-distinct-three-members
cases.description: three sequences that must all differ from each other within a row
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="env-d3" local="en" mode="memory"><distinct><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3,4"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3,4"/></sequence><sequence name="C"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3,4"/></sequence></distinct></env><block><line><data>${{A}}${{B}}${{C}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-simple-list
cases.description: 5 rows over a 5-value list — every value exactly once, order is the draw
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="u" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="G" uniq="true"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c,d,e"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{G}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-simple-int-range
cases.description: 12 distinct integers out of 1..40, drawn then never repeated
cases.config: <tdc><env count="12" seed="u" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="G" uniq="true"><gen type="number" value="1..40"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{G}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-simple-weighted-pack
cases.description: 10 first names from the weighted en pack, no repeats — the draw is without replacement
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="u" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="G" uniq="true"><gen type="template" value="person.male.firstName"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{G}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-group-with-a-mix-member
cases.description: A <mix> inside an env-level <uniq> is a member like any other: a group rearranges whole columns between rows, and a mix keeps its value multiset whatever the order, so its percentages survive the move. Before this case the name was not registered at all — every reference to it read as undeclared.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="mixgroup" local="en" mode="memory"><uniq><mix name="K" percent="50,50"><case><gen type="text" value="A"/></case><case><gen type="text" value="B"/></case></mix><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..4"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{K}}${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-group-with-a-switch-member
cases.description: A <switch> may join a group, but the group may only move its value between rows that share the subject: a male name must not land in a female row. Rows are partitioned by the subject and rearranged inside each block, so the tuple is unique across all rows AND every value still answers its own row's subject. RE-BASELINED 2026-08-04, and the old value is worth recording: it read M-ann-1 M-bob-3 F-cat-2 F-cat-3 — cat twice and dot never. The subject M,F over four rows is an exact 2/2, so the two F rows draw from a two-value list and must take one of each. They did not, because every <switch> branch used to be built over the WHOLE run and only the rows that chose it survived; a branch could therefore repeat itself and skip a value. This case was pinning that fault. The description also claimed three F rows and one M, which the config never produced. RE-BASELINED A SECOND TIME the same day, for the ORDER within the F block: it read F-dot-3 F-cat-2 and now reads F-cat-3 F-dot-2. Once a branch draws over its own rows, those rows have an order, and it is not row order — it is the rank inside the subject's exact layout, the same order parent="G.F" uses. The first fix numbered them by row instead, which put the right values on the wrong rows and made engine 1 and engine 3 disagree. What settles which value is right is not a comparison against the parent= form — a branch draws on its own stream name, so within the subset it arranges values differently from a sequence of another name. It is that engine 1 and engine 3 now produce this line and before produced two different ones from the same seed.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="switchgroup" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="M,F"/></sequence><uniq><switch name="N" on="G"><case is="M"><gen type="text" value="ann,bob"/></case><case is="F"><gen type="text" value="cat,dot"/></case></switch><sequence name="S"><gen type="number" value="1..4"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{G}}-${{N}}-${{S}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-true-and-uniq-True-mean-the-same-thing
cases.description: Every other boolean attribute in the DSL is read case-insensitively; uniq alone was compared against the bare lowercase literal, so `uniq="True"` validated as a uniqueness promise and then drew with replacement. Both columns here exhaust the same eight values, and they must agree — a port that keeps the strict comparison produces duplicates in the second column only.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="s" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="Lower" uniq="true"><gen type="number" value="1..8"/></sequence><sequence name="Upper" uniq="True"><gen type="number" value="1..8"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{Lower}},${{Upper}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-switch-in-a-distinct-group-is-redrawn-inside-its-own-branch
cases.description: An env-level <distinct> redraws a colliding member until it differs. A <switch> member has to be redrawn inside the branch its subject chose — a p row must come back with another p value. The redraw had no row to select a branch with, so it produced the empty string, which the caller accepted as different from everything and wrote into the cell: colliding rows came out blank on every engine, with no diagnostic, from a config the docs describe as supported. The bracketed column pins that the value is present, not merely different.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="8" seed="dsw" local="en"><sequence name="K"><gen type="text" value="p,q"/></sequence><distinct><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="x,y,z"/></sequence><switch name="B" on="K"><case is="p"><gen type="text" value="x,y,z"/></case><case is="q"><gen type="text" value="x,y,z"/></case></switch></distinct></env><block><line><data>${{K}} ${{A}} [${{B}}]</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-uniq-group-a-switch-cuts-into-blocks
cases.description: A <switch> in a <uniq> cuts the rows into blocks by its subject, and the free members are DEALT across those blocks in equal shares before anything is arranged inside them. Without the deal a block gets whichever values fell into it — one came out [7,3,4] where an even share is [5,5,4] — and the run is refused for want of data it has. Three counts here: one the old builder managed, and two it did not.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="blocks" local="en" mode="memory"><uniq><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="M,F" percent="50,50"/></sequence><switch name="N" on="G"><case is="M"><gen type="text" value="m1,m2,m3"/></case><case is="F"><gen type="text" value="f1,f2,f3"/></case></switch><sequence name="L"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c,d,e"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{G}}|${{N}}|${{L}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-block-order-is-the-order-the-subjects-appear
cases.description: The deal breaks a tie by BLOCK ORDER, so the order the blocks are made in is part of the contract. It was not until the deal existed — each block used to be arranged from its own values, so their order never showed — and one implementation was keeping them sorted by subject instead. An odd count is what tells the two apart: the block that appears first gets the extra value.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="7" seed="blocks" local="en" mode="memory"><uniq><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="M,F" percent="50,50"/></sequence><switch name="N" on="G"><case is="M"><gen type="text" value="m1,m2"/></case><case is="F"><gen type="text" value="f1,f2"/></case></switch><sequence name="L"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c,d"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{G}}|${{N}}|${{L}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-switched-mix-inside-a-uniq-group
cases.description: The shape Studio's medical demo has: the group holds a <switch> whose branches are each a <mix> with shares of their own. The deal must leave both alone — the switched column and the subject the blocks were cut by — while still giving the free member a fair share.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="12" seed="blocks" local="en" mode="memory"><uniq><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="M,F" percent="50,50"/></sequence><switch name="N" on="G"><case is="M"><gen type="text" value="m1,m2"/></case><case is="F"><gen type="text" value="f1,f2"/></case></switch><sequence name="L"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c"/></sequence><switch name="D" on="G"><case is="M"><mix percent="50"><case><gen type="text" value="dm"/></case><case><gen type="text" value="g1"/></case></mix></case><case is="F"><mix percent="50"><case><gen type="text" value="df"/></case><case><gen type="text" value="g1"/></case></mix></case></switch></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{G}}|${{N}}|${{L}}|${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: every-seed-reaches-the-ceiling-the-data-holds
cases.description: The deal's remainder tie used to go to block 0 every time, so WHETHER a count near the top collected depended on the seed: this exact shape at 24 collected on four seeds of eight. Ties now break by the most room left, and the shape's true ceiling — 3 names × 5 letters per block, 30 rows — is reached from any seed. Pinned at the ceiling itself, where every misdeal shows.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="30" seed="blocks" local="en"><uniq><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="M,F" percent="50,50"/></sequence><switch name="F" on="G"><case is="M"><gen type="text" value="m1,m2,m3"/></case><case is="F"><gen type="text" value="f1,f2,f3"/></case></switch><sequence name="L"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c,d,e"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{G}}|${{F}}|${{L}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-plain-pack-is-laid-out-not-picked
cases.description: A plain pack — a value list with no weights — is laid out in equal shares over the column and permuted, exactly as a plain text list is. A per-row pick left every value's count to chance, and inside a <uniq> that chance decided whether the run collects: this shape used to refuse at 12 saying 'at most 10'. 16 directions × 2 gives 32 combinations; 12 rows collect from any draw that is actually even.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="12" seed="p" local="en"><uniq><sequence name="C"><gen type="template" value="geo.direction"/></sequence><sequence name="D"><gen type="text" value="1,2"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{C}}|${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-plain-file-list-is-laid-out-not-picked
cases.description: A plain file list takes the same exact-layout road as a plain text list and a plain pack. Five fruits over ten rows is exactly two of each; a per-row pick gave some fruit four rows and another none, and a <uniq> over this shape was a coin flip.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="10" seed="f" local="en"><uniq><sequence name="A"><gen type="file" src="five-fruits.txt"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="text" value="x,y"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{A}}|${{B}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-odd-count-near-the-ceiling-collects
cases.description: An odd count cuts the blocks 13/12, and a per-value deal starved the smaller one: every value's remainder favours the 13, block 0 filled after four values, the fifth landed [1,4], and count 25 was refused saying 'at most 24' — on most seeds. The deal now hands its leftover units out globally, strongest claim first, so no block can be starved, and 25 collects on every seed.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="25" seed="blocks" local="en"><uniq><sequence name="G"><gen type="text" value="M,F" percent="50,50"/></sequence><switch name="F" on="G"><case is="M"><gen type="text" value="m1,m2,m3"/></case><case is="F"><gen type="text" value="f1,f2,f3"/></case></switch><sequence name="L"><gen type="text" value="a,b,c,d,e"/></sequence></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{G}}|${{F}}|${{L}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-regex-plate
cases.description: uniq over a regex pattern, the way it is meant to be used: a plate number, every row a different one. Refused as "cannot be enumerated" until 0.3.3 — a pattern was never enumerated and never needed to be; the integer range beside it redraws on a repeat, and so does this.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="50" seed="regex-plate" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="regex" value="[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-regex-whole-space
cases.description: All hundred strings of [0-9]{2}, once each. The worst case for redrawing: by the last few rows nearly every draw is a repeat, so this pins the exact sequence of redraws five implementations have to take, not just that they finish.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="100" seed="regex-whole" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="regex" value="[0-9]{2}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-regex-variable-length
cases.description: [a-c]{1,3} holds 3 + 9 + 27 = 39 strings and all 39 are asked for. Each length is picked one time in three, so the three one-letter strings run out almost at once and the rest of the column is longer — uniqueness bends the length mix, it does not refuse it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="39" seed="regex-var" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="regex" value="[a-c]{1,3}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-regex-backreference
cases.description: ([ab])\1-[0-9] is 2 · 10 = 20 strings, not 40: a back-reference repeats a group already counted. All twenty, once each.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="regex-backref" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="regex" value="([ab])\1-[0-9]"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-advanced-regex-shares
cases.description: 70/30 shares that must stay exact while every row differs. RU is 91 of 130 rows from the 100 strings that start RU-, so nearly every late RU draw repeats and is redrawn along the RU branch — never moved to US, which would break the share.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="130" seed="adv-shares" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="advanced_regex" value="(?%{70:RU;30:US})-[0-9]{2}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-advanced-regex-whole-space
cases.description: Both shares filled completely: ten A strings and ten B strings, all twenty asked for.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="adv-whole" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="advanced_regex" value="(?%{50:A;50:B})[0-9]"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-advanced-regex-conditional
cases.description: A conditional reads a weighted group. M rows take [a-c] and F rows [x-z], thirty strings a side and all sixty asked for — after every redraw the letter still agrees with the group.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="60" seed="adv-cond" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="advanced_regex" value="(?<s>(?%{50:M;50:F}))-(?if{s=M:[a-c];s=F:[x-z]})[0-9]"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-advanced-regex-nested
cases.description: Nested weighted choices: 5 a, 5 b and 10 c out of 20, each share counted along both branches it took, the c share filled exactly.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="adv-nested" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="advanced_regex" value="(?%{50:(?%{50:a;50:b});50:c})[0-9]"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-advanced-regex-in-repeat
cases.description: A weighted choice inside {2} deals twice per row, exactly at each step. A redraw has to meet it twice again and take the branches it was dealt both times.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="30" seed="adv-repeat" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="advanced_regex" value="((?%{50:a;50:b})){2}[0-9]"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-advanced-regex-under-alternation
cases.description: A weighted choice under a free alternation. A redraw that wanders to the other side meets a different set of weighted choices and is thrown away — this pins how far each implementation draws before it notices, which is what keeps the five on the same stream.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="60" seed="adv-alt" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="advanced_regex" value="(x|(?%{50:a;50:b}))[0-9]{2}"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: uniq-advanced-regex-twin-choices
cases.description: Two weighted choices written the SAME way, one on each side of an alternation. A redraw that crosses sides meets the other choice at the same point in its walk, and must be thrown away rather than read as the choice its row was dealt — so the two are told apart by identity. An implementation that compared them by value (a record, a dataclass) would move rows between the sides and break both shares, and this case would say so. Twenty rows fit whatever way the sides fall: one side could take all twenty and still split them ten and ten into branches of ten strings each.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="20" seed="adv-twins" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="V" uniq="true"><gen type="advanced_regex" value="(x(?%{50:a;50:b})|y(?%{50:a;50:b}))[0-9]"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{V}}</data></line></block></tdc>
